references.text: The Lord's anger was kindled against Israel because of their apostasy, reflecting the same theme of God's wrath over his children's unfaithfulness.
God heard and became angry, and he completely rejected Israel. The same motif of God's rejection of his people due to their sin.
Isaiah describes how the Lord has raised sons and daughters who have rebelled against him, reflecting the theme of God's disappointment with his children.
The Lord has rejected and abandoned the generation on whom he is angry. The same theme of God's rejection of his people because of their wickedness.
The Lord has rejected his altar and abhorred his sanctuary. This shows God's contempt and rejection in response to the people's sin.
Ezekiel describes Israel's unfaithfulness as children of parents who despised their spouses and children, reflecting the theme of sons and daughters provoking God.
Citing how God became angry with the wilderness generation and swore that they would not enter his rest. A direct reference to God's wrath over Israel in the wilderness.
